items.t: Black Holes and Their Mysterious Bright Structures Explained

items.t: Did The First Quarks and Gluons Experience Brownian Motion? Sometimes.

items.t: This Rare Binary Star Emits Radio Pulses Every Few Minutes. Will It Eventually Explode?
items.sum: Astronomers have found a Long Period Radio Transient about 5,000 light years away that's different from other LPTs. Other LPTs have a white dwarf and a red dwarf, but this one has a white dwarf and a main sequence star. The exact cause of the binary pair's radio pulses isn't certain, but this work narrows it down. It also shows that these binaries could be common progenitors for Type Ia supernova explosions.

items.t: Astrophysicists Cross Another Dark Matter Candidate Off Their List: Stupendously Large Black Holes
items.sum: Astrophysicists are leaving no stone unturned in their search for what dark matter is. Different particles have been proposed, like WIMPs and axions. Hypothetical rimordial black holes have also been proposed. But there's another less well-known candidate, SLABs or Stupendously Large Black holes, a sub-type of primordial black holes. Alas, SLABs can't account for dark matter either, according to new research.

items.t: Dense Galaxy Clusters Foster Mechanisms That Throttle Star Formation
